vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where you buy and eat meals
vocabulary.example: Let's try the new Italian restaurant.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small place that serves coffee, drinks and light meals
vocabulary.note_ar: من الفرنسية؛ العلامة فوق e أصبحت اختيارية: cafe
vocabulary.example: We met at a café near the station.
vocabulary.note_en: From French; the accent on the e is now optional: cafe.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a simple, cheap restaurant, often open all day (US)
vocabulary.note_ar: شائع في أمريكا، وقد تعني أيضاً «شخص يتناول الطعام»
vocabulary.example: We had pancakes at a roadside diner.
vocabulary.note_en: Common in the US; it can also mean "a person who is eating a meal".

vocabulary.meaning_en: food that is cooked and served very quickly
vocabulary.example: Try not to eat fast food every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a meal where you serve yourself from many dishes
vocabulary.example: The hotel has a breakfast buffet.
vocabulary.note_en: American: /bəˈfeɪ/, British: /ˈbʊfeɪ/; the t is silent.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a man / woman who serves food in a restaurant
vocabulary.example: The waitress brought us the menu.
vocabulary.note_en: "Waiter" for a man and "waitress" for a woman.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a professional cook in a restaurant
vocabulary.example: The chef came out to greet the guests.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of the food you can order
vocabulary.example: Can we see the menu, please?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper showing how much you must pay
vocabulary.example: Could we have the bill, please?
vocabulary.note_en: "Bill" is British, "check" is American.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an arrangement to keep a table, seat or room for you
vocabulary.example: I made a reservation at Bella's for eight o'clock.
vocabulary.note_en: make a reservation at + place

vocabulary.meaning_en: an official arrangement to have a seat, room or ticket
vocabulary.example: Your hotel booking is confirmed.
vocabulary.note_en: From the verb "book".

vocabulary.meaning_en: extra money added to the bill for the service
vocabulary.example: A 12% service charge is included.
vocabulary.note_en: If there is a service charge, you don't need to leave a tip.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extra money you give a waiter to thank them
vocabulary.example: We left a good tip because the service was great.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a dish the restaurant offers only for a short time
vocabulary.example: Today's special is grilled fish.
vocabulary.note_en: "Today's special" = the dish the restaurant offers today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small dish eaten before the main course
vocabulary.note_ar: appetizer أمريكي (من appetite = شهية)، starter بريطاني (يبدأ به الأكل)
vocabulary.example: We shared some appetizers before dinner.
vocabulary.note_en: "Appetizer" is American (from appetite); "starter" is British (you start the meal with it).

vocabulary.meaning_en: UK: a starter; US: the main dish
vocabulary.note_ar: في بريطانيا = مقبّلات، وفي أمريكا = الطبق الرئيسي
vocabulary.example: For my entrée, I'll have the steak. (US)
vocabulary.note_en: In Britain it means a starter; in the US it means the main course.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the biggest and most important dish of a meal
vocabulary.example: For the main course, I'll have chicken.
vocabulary.note_en: Understood everywhere.

vocabulary.meaning_en: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
vocabulary.example: I'm too full for dessert.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a drink (formal word)
vocabulary.note_ar: اسم فقط ورسمية أكثر من drink، ولا تُطلق عادةً على الماء
vocabulary.example: Hot beverages are served in the lounge.
vocabulary.note_en: Only a noun, and more formal than "drink". It is not usually used for water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of cloth or paper for cleaning your mouth and hands while eating
vocabulary.example: Put the napkin on your lap.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a flat round dish that you put food on
vocabulary.example: Be careful, the plate is hot.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a prepared meal; also any container used for food
vocabulary.note_ar: the dishes = كل أواني المطبخ: wash/do the dishes
vocabulary.example: Koshari is a famous Egyptian dish.
vocabulary.note_en: "The dishes" = all the plates, cups and pots you used: wash/do the dishes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with points used for eating
vocabulary.example: Can I have a fork and a knife?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with a small bowl used for eating soup
vocabulary.example: You need a spoon for this soup.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with a sharp edge for cutting
vocabulary.example: This knife is too sharp.
vocabulary.note_en: The k is silent: /naɪf/. Plural: knives.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a flat board for carrying food or drinks
vocabulary.example: The waiter carried six glasses on a tray.

vocabulary.meaning_en: food you buy to eat somewhere else
vocabulary.note_ar: UK: Eat in or take away?  US: For here or to go?
vocabulary.example: Can I get a coffee to go?
vocabulary.note_en: UK: Eat in or take away?  US: For here or to go?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long table where customers are served or pay
vocabulary.example: Please order at the counter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something very bad that causes a lot of trouble
vocabulary.example: The party was a complete disaster.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an informal word for friends or a group of people
vocabulary.example: Hey guys, are you ready?
vocabulary.note_en: Informal; used with friends.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a liquid fall out of its container by accident
vocabulary.example: I spilled juice on the carpet.
vocabulary.note_en: spill - spilled/spilt

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who is visiting or is invited
vocabulary.example: We have guests coming for dinner.
vocabulary.note_en: The u is silent.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone remember something
vocabulary.example: Remind me to call my mother.
vocabulary.note_en: remind someone to (do something) / about (something)

vocabulary.meaning_en: slightly rude in a funny or cute way
vocabulary.note_ar: عامية بريطانية؛ cheeky monkey تقال للأطفال
vocabulary.example: That was a cheeky answer!
vocabulary.note_en: British slang; "cheeky monkey" is said to children.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not including
vocabulary.example: Everyone came except Tom.
vocabulary.note_en: Noun: exception.

vocabulary.meaning_en: almost
vocabulary.example: I nearly missed the bus.
vocabulary.note_en: Like "almost".

vocabulary.meaning_en: old (a polite word)
vocabulary.note_ar: ألطف وأكثر احتراماً من old عند وصف الأشخاص
vocabulary.example: This seat is reserved for elderly people.
vocabulary.note_en: Kinder and more respectful than "old" when describing people.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a machine for cooking food; a stove
vocabulary.example: The soup is on the cooker.
vocabulary.note_en: Careful: a cooker is a machine, not a person.

fine_lines.title: book vs reserve
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان بمعنى «يحجز». book أصلها من «كتاب» وتُستخدم للحجوزات الرسمية الموثّقة التي تسجّل فيها بياناتك في نظام، مثل تذاكر الطيران وغرف الفنادق. reserve لحجز مبدئي غير رسمي بالضرورة، مثل حجز طاولة في مطعم أو أن تطلب من البائع أن يحتفظ لك بقطعة، وكذلك المقاعد المخصّصة لفئة معيّنة.

examples.sentence: I booked a flight to London.
She booked a hotel room online.
I'd like to reserve a table for two at 5 p.m.
This seat is reserved for elderly passengers.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean to arrange a place or service in advance. "Book" comes from the word for a book, and is used for official bookings where your details go into a system, like plane tickets and hotel rooms. "Reserve" is for a less formal hold, like a table at a restaurant or asking a shop to keep an item for you; it is also used for seats kept for a certain group.

fine_lines.title: plate vs dish
fine_lines.explanation_ar: plate هو الطبق نفسه كإناء. dish هو الوجبة أو الأكلة التي داخل الطبق. أما the dishes بالجمع فمصطلح شامل لكل أواني المطبخ (أطباق، أكواب، ملاعق، قدور)، لذلك نقول wash the dishes.

examples.sentence: He dropped a plate and it broke.
It's your turn to do the dishes.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A "plate" is the flat object you eat from. A "dish" is the food or meal on the plate. "The dishes" (plural) means all the kitchen things you used (plates, cups, spoons, pots), so we say "wash the dishes".

fine_lines.title: cook vs cooker
fine_lines.explanation_ar: cook فعل بمعنى يطبخ، وهي أيضاً اسم بمعنى الطبّاخ (الشخص). أما cooker فهو الجهاز الذي نطبخ عليه (الموقد). لا تقل He is a good cooker.

examples.sentence: My father is a great cook.
We bought a new gas cooker.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Cook" is a verb (to make food) and also a noun meaning the person who cooks. A "cooker" is the machine you cook on (a stove). Don't say "He is a good cooker."

fine_lines.title: on time vs in time
fine_lines.explanation_ar: on time تعني في الموعد بالضبط، لا قبله ولا بعده. in time تعني قبل الموعد بوقت كافٍ أو في الوقت المناسب قبل فوات الأوان.

examples.sentence: The train left on time at 9:00.
We got to the cinema in time to buy popcorn.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "On time" means at exactly the planned time, not before and not after. "In time" means early enough, before it is too late.

fine_lines.title: elderly vs old
fine_lines.explanation_ar: elderly كلمة مهذّبة تصف المرحلة العمرية (كبار السن) دون إساءة. old عند وصف شخص قد تبدو وقحة، فالأفضل استخدام elderly مع الناس.

examples.sentence: She helps an elderly neighbor with shopping.
This is a very old building.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Elderly" is a polite word for older people. Using "old" to describe a person can sound rude, so it is better to say "elderly" about people.

expressions.phrase: bite off more than you can chew
expressions.meaning_ar: يحمّل نفسه أكثر من طاقته / يتولى مهمة أكبر من قدرته
expressions.example: Don't take three courses at once; don't bite off more than you can chew.
expressions.meaning_en: to try to do more than you are able to

expressions.meaning_ar: يأخذ الأمور ببساطة / لا يُجهد نفسه (وقد تعني الاستهتار)
expressions.example: Why are you taking it so easy? The exam is tomorrow!
expressions.meaning_en: to relax and not work too hard (it can also mean not being serious enough)

expressions.example: Don't eat too much bread; save room for dessert.
expressions.meaning_en: to leave space in your stomach for dessert

expressions.meaning_ar: معك فلان (للتعريف بنفسك في الهاتف أو الرسائل)
expressions.example: Hello, this is Sara from the bank.
expressions.meaning_en: used to say who you are on the phone or in a message

expressions.example: I made a reservation at the hotel restaurant.
expressions.meaning_en: to book a table or place at (somewhere)

expressions.example: "For here or to go?" "To go, please."
expressions.meaning_en: Will you eat here or take the food away? (American)

grammar.title: Present perfect: breaking news
grammar.explanation_ar: الاستخدام الثالث للمضارع التام: «الأخبار العاجلة». عندما يحدث شيء الآن وله أثر واضح في الحاضر، نستخدم المضارع التام كأنه شريط أخبار عاجل. I have lost my keys تعني أنك الآن أمام الباب ولا تستطيع الدخول. أما I lost my keys فتحكي قصة حدث انتهى.
examples: I have broken my leg! (you can see it now)
I broke my leg two years ago.
I have lost my keys, and I can't get in.
grammar.explanation_en: The third use of the present perfect: "breaking news". When something just happened and has a clear result now, we use the present perfect, like a breaking news banner. "I have lost my keys" means you are at the door now and can't get in. "I lost my keys" just tells a story about a finished event.

grammar.title: Speaker's choice: past simple or present perfect
grammar.explanation_ar: في هذا الاستخدام أنت «المذيع» وتختار: المضارع التام يُبرز أهمية الخبر وأثره عليك الآن، والماضي البسيط يقدّمه كأمر عادي لا يهمّك كثيراً. ولا تربط just و already بالمضارع التام دائماً، فهما تأتيان مع الماضي البسيط أيضاً.
examples: I have washed the dishes! (proud, important news)
I washed the dishes. (a normal daily task)
I just spilled coffee on my shirt.
grammar.explanation_en: Here you are the "news reader" and you choose: the present perfect shows the news is important and affects you now; the past simple presents it as a normal fact that doesn't matter much. Also, "just" and "already" are not only used with the present perfect; they can go with the past simple too.

grammar.title: Starting a sentence with But / And
grammar.explanation_ar: يمكنك أن تبدأ الجملة بـ But أو And، وهذا شائع جداً في الكتابة والكلام. كان بعض المدرسين يمنعونه خوفاً من كتابة جمل ناقصة فقط.
examples: But please don't order ten appetizers again.
And I'm saving room for dessert.
grammar.explanation_en: You can start a sentence with "But" or "And". This is very common in both writing and speaking. Some teachers only banned it because they were afraid students would write incomplete sentences.

questions.question: I'd like to ___ a table for four at 8 p.m.
questions.explanation_ar: حجز طاولة في مطعم حجز مبدئي = reserve.
questions.explanation_en: Holding a table at a restaurant is a simple, informal booking = reserve.

questions.question: In the US, "entrée" means:
questions.explanation_ar: في أمريكا entrée هو الطبق الرئيسي، وفي بريطانيا المقبلات.
questions.explanation_en: In the US, an entrée is the main course; in Britain it is the starter.

questions.question: Which word means the machine you cook on?
questions.explanation_ar: cooker جهاز الطبخ، و cook الشخص الذي يطبخ.
questions.explanation_en: A cooker is the machine for cooking; a cook is the person who cooks.

questions.question: It's your turn to wash the ___.
questions.explanation_ar: the dishes مصطلح شامل لكل أواني المطبخ.
questions.explanation_en: "The dishes" means all the kitchen things you used.

questions.question: In American English, you ask for the ___ at the end of the meal.
You are standing outside your door and can't get in. You say:
questions.explanation_ar: خبر عاجل له أثر الآن: المضارع التام.
questions.explanation_en: Breaking news with a result right now: present perfect.

questions.question: "Don't bite off more than you can chew" means:
questions.explanation_ar: لا تحمّل نفسك أكثر من طاقتك.
questions.explanation_en: Don't try to do more than you are able to.

questions.question: The meeting starts at 10. He arrived at exactly 10. He arrived:
questions.explanation_en: On time = at exactly the planned time.

questions.question: Which is the most polite word for old people?
questions.explanation_ar: elderly كلمة مهذبة لوصف كبار السن.
questions.explanation_en: "Elderly" is a polite word for older people.

questions.question: Which word is formal and is not usually used for water?
questions.explanation_ar: beverage رسمية ولا تُطلق عادةً على الماء، و drink تشمل كل ما يُشرب.
questions.explanation_en: "Beverage" is formal and not usually used for water; "drink" covers everything you drink.
